messages:
Sara (PM): quick sync 0: prioritizing two private-deploy asks from sales: preserve customer egress IPs for long-lived tenants, and a zero-downtime upgrade path for air-gapped installs. what are minimal launch criteria?
Chen (Eng Lead): +1. propose M1 vs M2 split. M1 should guarantee egress IP preservation for operator-managed clusters and provide a documented scheduled-maintenance fallback. M2 can tackle live KV migration and blue-green network handoffs.
Diego (SRE): preserving egress IPs is mostly installer + operator affinity logic. zero-downtime is doable but KV cache migration is the trickiest bit. we should list three upgrade strategies and tradeoffs.
Maya (Field): acme and finco flagged both as blockers. Acme needs no-IP-change in cutover window <= 2h. they want an installer toggle rather than manual netops.
Lucas (Solutions): simple UX: `--preserve-egress` flag + `redwoodctl network-check` preflight script. provide sample netplan commands for common CPEs. customers want a dry-run that shows IP mapping changes.
Chen (Eng Lead): tech outline: ensure consistent node labels, deterministic host selection, graceful drain that keeps service endpoints stable. can be operator-side only. est: 3 sprints for M1 scope.
Diego (SRE): upgrade patterns: A) rolling with KV migration (complex), B) dual-read side-by-side (more resources), C) blue-green with VIP failover (safest for egress). small customers may not have resources for B/C.
Maya (Field): customers want C but may accept scheduled maintenance with IP-preserve checkpoints. need clear fallback guidance in runbook.
Sara (PM): propose launch buckets: M1 (GA): installer `--preserve-egress`, preflight + docs + troubleshooting scripts, validated rollback playbook. M2: VIP handoff blue-green, KV live migration, minimal-agent packaging for low-capacity sites. agree?
Chen (Eng Lead): agree on M1. will add operator labels + drain hooks. M2 needs research spike for KV migration.
Lucas (Solutions): I'll draft preflight UX and two `redwoodctl` sample runs for field demos. also prototype `minimal-agent` packaging ideas for M2.
Diego (SRE): need observability targets for upgrades: per-tenant latency checks, rollback thresholds, alert templates. I'll author an alert/playbook.
Maya (Field): will recruit 3 pilot customers (Acme, FinCo, EdgeHost) and run acceptance checklist. will capture netops runbook feedback.
Sara (PM): proposed M1 launch criteria:
- installer supports `--preserve-egress` and passes lab tests for common operator setups
- preflight that simulates egress handoff with deterministic output
- rollback playbook validated with 2 pilot customers
- public docs + runbook + support triage path
- telemetry: install success/failure + upgrade/rollback events emitted
If green -> signoff for M1 GA.
Chen (Eng Lead): CI targets: simulate edge NAT, host affinity scenarios, matrix of 3 network topologies.
Diego (SRE): canary plan: start with non-critical tenants, windows 30m, auto-rollback on error rates >2x baseline.
Sara (PM): owners: Chen->impl, Diego->rollout & playbook, Lucas->preflight UX & scripts, Maya->pilots, Sara->docs & comms. timeline: aim 3 sprints for M1.
Maya (Field): will schedule pilot cutovers and ask customers for preflight outputs. they requested a one-page slide for sales: 2 bullets (what we guarantee, prep recommended).
Lucas (Solutions): will post scripts + slide to #docs today.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: private-installer-v0.9.1 -> staging (build 482).
Chen (Eng Lead): note: document `--preserve-egress` limitations (HA, multi-AZ, operator downtime). avoid overpromising.
Sara (PM): agreed. include a limitations section in runbook and call out cost/scale tradeoffs.
Maya (Field): next sync Thurs 10am to review pilot results and CI pass status.
